reader.requirement: A user-defined name whose spelling (hyphens included) no other name shares is uniquely referenced without qualification; a spelling shared with another name is not, and needs SRL2.1's qualification.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Cite: only the citation text of the COBOL1639 ambiguity message (1985 IV.4.3.8.1 vs 2023 8.4.2.2.3 SR1); the verdict (one survivor resolves, several is an error) is the same code

ConstructRegistry.Check(QualifiedIndexName2002): a qualified index-name is refused at 85 (COBOL0900); 1985's qualification formats 1-6 name no index-name and VI.5.8.3 SR14 makes index-name-1 unique in the program

reader.edition-search: grep for DialectLevel, Edition.Year, EditionContext, CobolVersion, Permissive and ConstructRegistry in NameResolution.cs, SymbolTable.DataNameCandidates.cs, SymbolTable.IndexNames.cs, SymbolTable.Procedures.cs, SymbolTable.ConditionNames.cs, QualifiedNameClasses.cs, OccursKeyResolvePass.cs, OdoResolvePass.cs, StatementValidation.cs, DataBinder.cs#UniqueOrReportAmbiguous; the grammar rules qualification, dataReference, procedureName and reportGroupReference carry no version predicate
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: an unqualified reference resolves exactly when one declaration of the spelling is visible, at 85 as at 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb919 covers a duplicated index-name only; data-names, condition-names, procedure-names and hyphenation are not exercised

probes.printed: exit 0: HY NO DBL / XYZNO DBL
probes.expected: A-B, AB and A--B are three distinct names (spelling and hyphenation), each unique unqualified

probes.printed: exit 0: AAAA BBBB / CCCC DDDD / OK-R1-A OK-R1-B OK-R2-C OK-R2-D / 78 / 123 / CCCC / UNIQ / ZZZZZ / FFF12GGG34
probes.expected: every reference made unique by its qualifiers resolves to its own item: full and gapped chains, IN and OF mixed, record-name as data-name-1 and as qualifier, file-name qualifier, condition-names qualified by their conditional variable and its groups, subscripted qualified items, an unqualified unique name

probes.printed: exit 65, ten COBOL1639: X (2 match), X OF G (2 match), X OF R1 OF G (order), X OF T OF R1 (sibling not superordinate), UNIQ OF UNIQ, OK OF N OF R1 (not its conditional variable), OK (2 level-88s), FX OF GREC OF F1 (wrong file), FX (2), X OF R3 (no such qualifier)
probes.expected: each nonunique or misqualified reference refused (1985 IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.1, SRL2.4)

probes.printed: exit 65: COBOL6863 index-name 'IX' ... must be a unique word (1985 VI.5.8.3 SR14); COBOL1639 index-name reference 'IX' ... 2 declarations; COBOL0900 a qualified index-name requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: a duplicated index-name is refused and cannot be qualified at 85

probes.printed: exit 65: COBOL2121 PERFORM 'P1': the reference is not unique ... 2 times (S1, S2)
probes.expected: unqualified P1 from a third section is ambiguous (SRL2.1/SRL2.6)

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR1  the text is in SR1 (quoted: No other name has the identical spelling)

reader.notes: DataNameCandidates returns the whole candidate set of a spelling; one survivor resolves and several go to the one ambiguity verdict (COBOL1639). Spellings differing only in hyphenation (A-B, AB, A--B) are distinct names. Index-names at 85 are also unique by VI.5.8.3 SR14 (COBOL6863).

refuter.evidence: cn2.cob (runs/cn2-001): 'Abc' and 'ABC' in two records, MOVE to 'abc' -> COBOL1639 2 declarations; level-01 'r3' and 'R3' -> COBOL1639: case-folded spellings are one name. nest1.cob: a contained program's local X resolves unqualified beside a GLOBAL X, X OF GR reaches the global (LOC / GLB / GY / GY). The reader's hyph.cob covers hyphenation. cite: OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR1  the text is in SR1 (No other name has the identical spelling and hyphenation).
